morgan: Heads-up — noticed a host-side perf regression after last week's parse refactor. p50 host-side latency up ~12% for short sequences (<=64).

morgan: Quick profiler snapshot shows tokenize path and writev syscall spiking. KV-cache hits are fine, this looks pre-kv (parsing/tokenization/stream framing).

morgan: Repro script: `./tools/bench_ingress --type=http --qps=500 --seq=32 --batch=auto`

perf-bot: perf summary (top functions):
```
user   61.5%  tokenize_fragment
user   12.0%  parse_proto_frame
sys    10.8%  writev
user    5.5%  alloc_small
```

allegra: Oof. tokenize_fragment increase is surprising — that code didn't change much. Did we flip any allocator or copy strategy in the refactor?

jia: I pushed a tiny change to the parser to normalize chunk headers (1767fd). It replaced a single-scan state machine with a more generic scanner to handle edge cases — might have added extra bounds checks.

sam: Also saw more writev calls per request in traces — looks like streaming chunking now emits per-token frames for some inputs instead of coalescing.

morgan: Sample trace (trimmed):
```
INGRESS -> parse_frame (8µs)
parse_frame -> tokenize (45µs)
tokenize -> writev (3µs) [call #1]
tokenize -> writev (3µs) [call #2]
```

allegra: So two writev calls where previously we had one. That doubles syscall overhead for small messages. For high QPS that stacks.

jia: Confirmed — the new scanner returns token-by-token slightly earlier to simplify state, which lets the streaming layer flush more frequently. I can change it to expose a "batch available" hint so the framer coalesces.

sam: Another angle: batching heuristics. With many small requests, our auto-batcher chooses small batch sizes (<=4) — that combined with per-token flush is bad. We could bias batching to prefer coalescing across microbursts for hosts with high writev cost.

morgan: Actionable plan: 1) Jia adds batch-hint to parser to allow framer to coalesce; 2) Allegra trials a conservative bias in batching heuristic (min_batch_delay 250µs) behind a config flag; 3) Sam adds a writev coalescer util to avoid multiple small vectored writes; 4) Run canary.

jia: I'll send a small patch tonight: keep current token boundary semantics but add a `bool more_in_frame` hint and a fast path that returns a slice view instead of allocating a new buffer.

allegra: I'll wire the heuristic flag as `host.ingress.coalesce_delay_us` in flags for Dedicated hosts only, default 0. If perf wins, we can toggle for hosted quick.

sam: writev coalescer notes: we can accumulate up to 8 iovecs before triggering a syscall; use pre-allocated iovec array per-conn to avoid allocs. Also prefer net.Buffers-like path to combine adjacent slices.

morgan: Can we test locally quickly? Jia/Allegra — try this patchset:
1) parser-batch-hint branch: `git checkout parser-batch-hint && cargo build --release`
2) coalesce delay = 250us in config
3) run `./tools/bench_ingress --type=grpc --qps=400 --seq=32 --conns=200`

jia: Running now. Quick numbers (w/ parser hint only): p50 host latency down from 62µs to 52µs for seq=32, writev count per request unchanged though.

sam: Add writev coalescer patch (local): reduces writev syscalls from ~2.1 to ~1.02 per request. Combined with hint gives p50 ~45µs, p95 ~180µs (was 240µs).

perf-bot: perf after combined patches:
```
user   48.0%  tokenize_fragment (reduced)
sys     6.3%  writev (reduced)
user    8.5%  parse_proto_frame
```

allegra: Nice. Also check memory churn — we need to ensure slice-view path doesn't pin large buffers or increase KV cache churn.

jia: Slice view uses borrowed bytes from the connection read buffer; I added a short-lifetime wrapper so we don't hold onto the big buffer across async await points. No allocs observed in hot path.

morgan: Regression root cause summary: parser refactor introduced earlier token emission + extra allocations which exposed streaming framer to flush more frequently. Combined with unchanged batching heuristics this increased syscall overhead.

morgan: Risks: coalescing delay increases latency tail for some clients. We'll gate on host tier and run canary.

allegra: Can we add an experiment metric: host.ingress.coalesce_delay_us + p50/p95 + per-request writev_count exported to console, so SRE can watch?

sam: I'll add metrics: `ingress.writev.count`, `ingress.coalesce.delays` and a trace tag `coalesce_enabled=true/false`.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: dedicated-us-west-2 cluster, 10% traffic, start 2026-03-19T03:00Z -> 2h window. PRs: r/redwood/ingress#482, r/redwood/runtime#391.

jia: I'll open PR for parser hint (w/ tests) in ~30m. Sam/Allegra — want code reviews?

sam: Yep, will review. Also let's add a small microbenchmark under tools/bench to lock in numbers.

morgan: Thanks all. If canary looks good we'll roll to 100% and backfill a short postmortem note in incidents/ if anything surprising pops up. :thumbsup:

allegra: FYI: I also noticed a secondary hotspot in alloc_small coming from log formatting during high qps — switching to sampling logs reduced that by ~30% in my runs. I'll file a follow-up.

morgan: Great catch. Ok team, triage in two lanes: immediate deployable patches (parser hint + writev coalescer + metrics) and follow-ups (batch heuristics tweak + log sampling).

jia: PR link: https://git.re/redwood/ingress/pull/482 (WIP).
